sponsor: Harvard University (Harvard University Student Health Program, HUSHP)
administrator: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Massachusetts, Inc. (administrative services only; "Blue Cross and Blue Shield is not an underwriter or insurer of the benefits provided by this health plan")
_funding_note: Schema enum (data/schemas/README.md) offers 'self-funded-erisa | insured | medicare-part-d | medicare-advantage'. None applies: the Benefit Description (8-1-2026 ed., Introduction, p.1) states this is a 'non-insured, self-funded health benefits plan ... financed by contributions by the group.' A university plan covering students is not an ERISA employee welfare benefit plan (ERISA sec. 3(1), 29 U.S.C. 1002(1) — no employment-based coverage relationship). Enum extension 'self-funded-non-erisa' needs a logged decision in docs/DECISIONS.md.
plan_year_span: 2026-08-01 through 2027-07-31 (plan year runs August 1 - July 31; Benefit Description p.18; Summary p.5)

Stored (gitignored) at data/uploads/hushp/. Page cites below use the PRINTED page numbers (Schedule of Benefits pages are cited 'SoB p.N'; body pages 'p.N').

regulatory_regime.summary: Self-funded, non-insured student health plan sponsored by a university and administered by BCBSMA under an administrative-services contract. It is NOT an ERISA plan (no employment relationship; ERISA sec. 3(1), 29 U.S.C. 1002(1)), and it is NOT 'student health insurance coverage' under 45 CFR 147.145 (that rule reaches only issuer-provided individual coverage). Member protections below are therefore chiefly CONTRACTUAL (plan-document) terms, many of which deliberately mirror ACA/DOL claims and external-review standards; the appeal section's exhaustion-exception wording tracks 45 CFR 147.136 / 29 CFR 2590.715-2719 almost verbatim.

applicable.regime: Plan contract governed by Massachusetts law except as preempted by federal law
MA student health program mandate and program standards
MA Minimum Creditable Coverage — plan states it meets MCC standards
applicable.cite: SMB p.6 disclaimer; M.G.L. c. 111M; 956 CMR 5.00

applicable.regime: Self-funded student health coverage as minimum essential coverage
Surprise-billing protections described in the plan document as 'under federal law'
applicable.cite: BD pp.7-8 (No Surprises Act-style protections); statutory applicability to a non-ERISA student plan is contractual/mixed

not_applicable.cite: 29 CFR 2560.503-1 — inapplicable; not an employee welfare benefit plan
inapplicable; commercial student plan. A rep quoting Part D 72-hour/24-hour coverage-determination clocks to this member is answering from the wrong regime.
45 CFR 147.145 — defines student health insurance coverage as issuer-provided individual coverage; this plan is self-funded, not issuer coverage

not_applicable.regime: MA Office of Patient Protection external review for carrier products
not_applicable.cite: 958 CMR 3.000 applies to insured carrier products; this plan's external review is a contractual process through an external review agency (BD pp.84-86). UNVERIFIED whether OPP accepts HUSHP SHIP appeals — do not grade a rep wrong solely for not mentioning OPP.

deductible_individual_out_of_network.value: $250 per member / $500 per family per plan year, out-of-network only (applies to all out-of-network benefits except as noted in the Schedule; in-network spending does not accrue to it)

oop_max_medical_in_network.value: $1,700 per member / $3,400 per family per plan year (deductible+copays+coinsurance; EXCLUDES prescription-drug cost share)

oop_max_medical_out_of_network.value: $7,500 per member / $15,000 per family per plan year; in-network and out-of-network accruals do not cross-apply; balance-billed excess charges are on top

oop_max_rx.value: Separate prescription-drug out-of-pocket maximum: $1,300 per member / $2,600 per family per plan year

oop_max_combined_presentation.value: The AY2026-27 Summary presents in-network OOP max as '$3,000 per member / $6,000 per family (Combined medical and prescription)' — arithmetic of $1,700+$1,300 and $3,400+$2,600. A rep quoting either $1,700 (medical-only) or $3,000 (combined) can be correct; a rep quoting $3,000 as medical-only, or unable to explain the split, is materially misleading (Warning).

pcp_cost_share.value: $35 copayment per office/health-center/home visit in-network; 30% after deductible out-of-network. No separate PCP-vs-specialist tiering. Copay waived for in-network OB/GYN physician/nurse-practitioner services; waived for members age 17 or younger seen by any Atrius provider. Note: most routine/primary care for enrolled students is delivered at HUHS under the Student Health Fee at $0 (SMB pp.2-5), outside SHIP cost share.

specialist_cost_share.value: $35 copayment per visit in-network (same 'Medical Care Outpatient Visits' row as PCP; Summary labels it 'diagnostic/specialist/sick'); 30% after deductible out-of-network. No referral needed (see referral_required).

er_cost_share.value: $100 copayment per emergency-room visit; copayment WAIVED if held for observation or admitted within 24 hours. Out-of-network ER: same as in-network benefits (deductible does not apply). Worldwide emergency coverage; no referral or approval needed for emergency care.
er_cost_share.regime_note: Cost share is PLAN; ER coverage without prior approval including out-of-network parity mirrors federal/MA emergency-access standards

urgent_care_cost_share.value: $35 copayment in-network (urgent care centers are covered providers billed as outpatient medical care visits); 30% after deductible out-of-network. HUHS urgent care is covered in full by the Student Health Fee (after-hours line 617-495-5711).
urgent_care_cost_share.page: SMB p.6; BD p.12 (covered providers); HB p.23

inpatient_hospital_cost_share.value: $100 copayment per admission at most network general hospitals; $500 per admission at Hospital Choice Cost Sharing higher-tier hospitals (per 2024-edition rider: base + $400; list includes MGH, Brigham & Women's, Boston Children's, Dana-Farber, Baystate, Cape Cod, Fairview, UMass Memorial; ER-direct admissions get the lower tier). 30% after deductible out-of-network.
inpatient_hospital_cost_share.page: SoB p.2 and * footnote (SoB p.9); HCCS rider (BD24 rider pages 1-2)
inpatient_hospital_cost_share.caveat: The posted 8-1-2026 PDF references the HCCS Rider but does not attach it; hospital list taken from the 8-1-2024 edition's attached rider — verify current-year rider before grading hospital-tier answers.

mental_health_outpatient.value: In-network outpatient mental health/substance-use visits: no charge for first 8 visits per plan year, then $35 copayment per visit; 30% after deductible out-of-network.

rx_tier_2_retail.value: $40 copayment, Tier 2 (preferred brand), retail, per 30-day supply

rx_mail_order.value: Designated mail-order pharmacy, 90-day supply: $51 / $120 / $165 (Tiers 1/2/3). Cost share waived for Tier 1 birth-control drugs/devices, certain preventive drugs required by federal law, certain orally-administered anticancer drugs (retail also waives insulin-infusion pumps and glucometers).
rx_mail_order.regime_note: Copays PLAN; $0 preventive/contraceptive waivers track federal preventive-services requirements

rx_out_of_network.value: Out-of-network pharmacy: NOT covered — member pays all charges (limited paper-claim exceptions for non-network purchases per BD Part 5).

rx_retail_supply_limit_CONFLICT.value: CONFLICT: Schedule of Benefits (8-1-2026) says retail = 30-day supply; the AY2026-27 Summary says retail = 'up to a 60-day formulary supply for each prescription or refill'. Benefit Description governs by the Summary's own disclaimer, but this is a live discrepancy in Harvard's current materials — a strong audit probe. Grade against 30-day (BD) while flagging.

rx_administrator.value: Prescription benefits are administered by BCBSMA as part of the plan (BCBSMA Drug Formulary; BCBSMA-designated mail-order pharmacy; BCBSMA-designated retail specialty pharmacy for certain specialty drugs). No outside PBM is named anywhere in the plan documents. Handbook: 'SHIP provides hospital, specialty care, and prescription drug benefits through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts.'
rx_administrator.caveat: BCBSMA's back-end PBM subcontractor is not stated in any plan document — do not assert a vendor name on calls or in grading.

rx_prior_auth.value: Certain formulary drugs require prior approval from BCBSMA before coverage; 'a covered pharmacy will tell you if your drug needs prior approval ... they will also tell you how to request this approval.' Provider-administered drugs (office/outpatient infusions and injections) require pre-service approval, and step therapy is 'a key part of this pre-service approval process.'

step_therapy.value: Step therapy applies: before coverage is approved for certain 'second step' drugs, the member must first try an effective 'first step' drug. Defined under Utilization Review (p.20) and applied within pre-service drug approval (p.24).

formulary_exception_process.value: Drug Formulary Exception Process: the PRESCRIBING health care provider asks BCBSMA for coverage of a non-formulary drug; considered when there is a medical basis the member cannot take any covered or OTC alternative. If approved, the drug is covered at the non-preferred (Tier 3) cost share. No decision turnaround time is stated in the Benefit Description.
formulary_exception_process.caveat: 45 CFR 156.122(c) (72-hr standard / 24-hr expedited exception clocks) binds issuer coverage, not clearly this self-funded plan — do not grade a rep against those clocks without a plan-side source.

pa_required_services.value: Pre-service approval from BCBSMA required for: certain outpatient specialty care/procedures/supplies (e.g., some surgeries, non-emergency ground ambulance, certain outpatient treatment plans); infertility treatment; certain provider-administered drugs. Pre-admission review required for ALL non-emergency, non-maternity inpatient admissions. Exception: substance-use admissions at MA DPH-licensed/certified facilities need no prior approval for up to 14 days if the facility notifies BCBSMA within 48 hours. The PA list can change; check with provider, BCBSMA customer service, or bluecrossma.org member self-service.
pa_required_services.regime_note: PA scope is PLAN; the 14-day SUD no-PA exception mirrors MA substance-use access law

pa_initiator.value: A network health care provider requests pre-service approval ON THE MEMBER'S BEHALF, and BCBSMA treats the provider as the member's authorized representative — BUT the plan instructs: 'You must request this review if the health care provider does not start the process for you.' Correct rep answer: provider normally initiates; the member can and must trigger the review if the provider fails to. WRONG (Critical): 'you cannot do anything yourself' or 'you can get it approved without any provider involvement' (clinical information still comes from the provider). Members check status via provider or BCBSMA customer service (number on ID card).

pa_turnaround_standard.value: BCBSMA decides pre-service and pre-admission requests within 2 WORKING DAYS of receiving all needed information. Approvals: phone call to provider within 24 hours of decision + written/electronic notice within 2 working days of the call. Denials: phone call within 24 hours + written notice within 1 working day of the call, stating reasons, clinical basis, alternatives, criteria, and review rights.
pa_turnaround_standard.audit_note: NOT the Part D 72-hour/24-hour clocks and NOT the ERISA 15-day pre-service clock — a rep quoting those regimes here is answering the wrong plan type.

pa_missing_info_clock.value: If information is missing, BCBSMA requests it within 15 calendar days of the provider's PA request; the information must be returned within 45 calendar days or coverage is denied; decision within 2 working days of receipt.

pa_reconsideration.value: Provider may request reconsideration of an adverse medical-necessity determination; clinical peer review held within 1 working day of the request. Member may go straight to formal internal review regardless.

referral_required.value: NO referral required: 'You do not need a referral from your primary care provider or your attending physician in order for you to receive your health plan coverage.' (Certain services still need BCBSMA pre-service approval — a different thing.) Emergency care needs neither referral nor approval. A rep telling a member a referral is required to see a specialist is wrong (Warning; Critical if it deters care).

internal_appeal_window.value: Internal formal appeal/grievance must be RECEIVED by BCBSMA within 180 CALENDAR DAYS of the date of the treatment, event, or circumstance which is the cause of the dispute — the clock is anchored to the TREATMENT/EVENT DATE, not to receipt of a denial letter. Filing channels: mail (Member Appeal and Grievance Program, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts, One Enterprise Drive, Quincy, MA 02171-2126), fax 1-617-246-3616, email grievances@bcbsma.com, phone 1-800-472-2689. BCBSMA sends written confirmation of receipt within 15 calendar days.
internal_appeal_window.quote: All requests for an appeal or a grievance review must be received by Blue Cross and Blue Shield within 180 calendar days of the date of treatment, event, or circumstance which is the cause of your dispute
internal_appeal_window.audit_note: STRONGEST APPEALS TRAP IN THE PLAN — validates the non-ERISA finding operationally. A rep trained on ERISA group plans will very likely answer '180 days from the denial notice' (the 29 CFR 2560.503-1 standard), which is WRONG here and materially harmful: a member could believe the window is open when it closed months earlier measured from the service date. Grade 🔴 critical; cite BD p.82; do NOT cite ERISA. Recommended as a CORE question on every call.

internal_appeal_response_time.value: Internal formal review decided within 30 CALENDAR DAYS (extendable only by member agreement or while awaiting the member's medical-records authorization). EXPEDITED review for immediate/urgently-needed services: decision within 72 HOURS of the request 'or such shorter time period as required by federal law.' Previously-approved concurrent services continue during the review.

appeal_representative.value: Member may choose another person to act on their behalf during an appeal/grievance review and (except as otherwise described) must designate that person IN WRITING to BCBSMA; for urgent/emergency claims a health care professional with knowledge of the condition may act without written designation; conservator/POA/family member may act if the member cannot. For quality-of-care grievances, a signed release form must be returned before records are released.

external_review.value: Voluntary external review after an adverse internal decision: file within 4 MONTHS of receiving the internal denial letter, using the form provided with the letter. Case goes to an external review agency: standard decision within 45 DAYS of receipt; expedited within 72 HOURS. Expedited external review may be filed AT THE SAME TIME as an internal expedited review (urgent care situations / ongoing course of treatment; also inpatient/emergency continued-stay denials). Internal review may be bypassed where BCBSMA waives it, the situation is urgent, or BCBSMA failed to comply with internal-review requirements (with the de-minimis exception). External decision is final; if overturned, the notice states how and by when BCBSMA will pay/authorize. A rep saying 'there's nothing you can do after the appeal' is a Critical failure.
external_review.regime_note: Contractual process modeled nearly verbatim on the federal external-review rules (45 CFR 147.136(d); 29 CFR 2590.715-2719); NOT the MA OPP carrier process (958 CMR 3.000) — see regulatory_regime.

plan_discretion_clause.value: BCBSMA 'has full discretionary authority to interpret this benefit booklet'; determinations 'conclusive and binding unless ... arbitrary and capricious.' Legal action: internal formal review must be exhausted first (external review optional before suit); suit must be brought within 2 years after the cause of action arises ('Time Limit for Legal Action').

eligibility.value: Full-time or part-time Harvard students (per plan sponsor); spouses and dependent children to end of month of 26th birthday enrollable. Student Health Fee is mandatory for registered students enrolled more than half-time; SHIP is the BCBSMA-administered insurance component (waivable with comparable coverage per HUSHP rules). Coverage terms: Fall Aug 1-Jan 31, Spring Feb 1-Jul 31.
eligibility.page: BD pp.87-88; SMB p.1; HB pp.2, 19-21
eligibility.regime_note: Dependent-to-26 mirrors ACA; student mandate is MA law (M.G.L. c. 15A sec. 18)

network.value: PPO: Blue Care Elect / national BlueCard PPO network with Hospital Choice Cost Sharing tiering; out-of-network covered at 30% after deductible with balance-billing exposure (allowed-charge basis). Find a Doctor: bluecrossma.com/findadoctor, network 'PPO or EPO with Hospital Choice Cost Share Feature'.

secondary_payer_note.value: SHIP is 'almost always the secondary payor' when the member has other coverage; both cards must be presented; claims go to the primary plan first (BCBSMA Coordination of Benefits: 888-799-1888).

preventive_care_cost_share.value: In-network preventive care is generally No charge (routine medical exams, routine tests, routine GYN exams, routine Pap smear tests, family planning, routine hearing exams, newborn hearing screening). TWO EXCEPTIONS worth probing: routine VISION exams are $35 copayment per visit in-network (not free), and adult routine medical exams are NOT COVERED out-of-network. Pediatric preventive out-of-network is 30% after deductible.
preventive_care_cost_share.audit_note: Two traps: (1) 'all preventive is free' is wrong — routine vision is $35; (2) adult preventive is NOT covered out-of-network ('Not covered under this part'). 🟡 warning, 🔴 if the member is steered out-of-network for a routine physical.

oon_coverage.value: Out-of-network benefits exist but are separately and less generously structured: $250 deductible (vs $0 in-network), dominant 30%-after-deductible cost share, $7,500 OOP max (vs $1,700 in-network), and in-network/out-of-network accumulators DO NOT cross-apply (costs applied toward one 'will not be applied toward' the other). Some services not covered out-of-network at all (e.g., adult routine exams).
oon_coverage.page: SoB p.2 (deductible, OOP max, non-crossover); SoB pp.2-8 (30% pattern)
oon_coverage.audit_note: HIGH-VALUE: the non-crossover rule is the single most commonly botched call-center answer in PPO plans. A rep who says out-of-network costs count toward the in-network OOP max is 🔴 critical — member believes exposure caps at $1,700 when it is $7,500 plus balance billing.

rx_deductible.value: NO separate prescription-drug deductible is stated in the Schedule of Benefits (and the in-network medical deductible is $0, so no deductible gates in-network pharmacy). There IS a separate prescription-drug OUT-OF-POCKET MAXIMUM ($1,300), distinct from the $1,700 medical OOP max.
rx_deductible.audit_note: PREMISE-SENSITIVE: correct answer is a negative. The near-miss is real — a rep conflating the separate Rx OOP MAX with an 'Rx deductible' is 🟡 warning. Grade the distinction, not the keyword. Pairs with oop_max_combined_presentation.

external_review_window.value: External review must be filed within FOUR MONTHS after the member RECEIVES the denial letter from BCBSMA. External review is voluntary (not required before legal action). External review agency decides within 45 days of receipt (extendable with notice); expedited external review within 72 hours of the agency receiving the case.
external_review_window.quote: If you decide to request an external review, you must file your request within the four months after you receive the denial letter from Blue Cross and Blue Shield.
external_review_window.audit_note: Clock starts at RECEIPT of the denial letter. A rep quoting a shorter window (60 days is the common wrong answer, borrowed from other plans) is 🔴 critical — can cause forfeiture of appeal rights.

expedited_appeal_process.value: EXPEDITED internal review is available in place of standard internal review for immediate/urgently-needed services where waiting would seriously jeopardize life, health, or maximum-function recovery — or where the physician states the member would suffer severe pain that cannot be adequately managed without the care at issue. Decision within 72 HOURS of receipt (or shorter if federal law requires). The member may file an expedited EXTERNAL review AT THE SAME TIME as the internal expedited request (urgent care situations; ongoing course of treatment).
expedited_appeal_process.page: BD p.84 (internal expedited); BD p.85 (simultaneous external)
expedited_appeal_process.audit_note: TWO gradeable elements: the 72-hour clock AND the simultaneous-filing right — reps miss the second; 'you must finish the internal appeal first' is 🔴 critical in urgent situations. Physician-attested severe pain as an independent trigger is a third probe. REGIME CAUTION: 72 hours coincidentally matches the Part D expedited clock — same number, wrong authority; cite BD p.84, never 42 CFR.

grievance_process.value: Internal formal appeal or grievance may be filed in writing, by e-mail (grievances@bcbsma.com), or by phone (Member Appeal and Grievance Program). Deadline: received within 180 calendar days of the treatment/event/circumstance (see internal_appeal_window). BCBSMA confirms receipt in writing within 15 calendar days. A grievance (distinct from an appeal) covers complaints about care or service quality; quality-of-care grievances against a provider are investigated only with the member's permission.
grievance_process.page: BD p.82 (deadline, channels, acknowledgment); BD p.83 (grievance vs appeal, permission)

escalation_path.value: Appeals and grievances go to a dedicated unit — the Member Appeal and Grievance Program (1-800-472-2689, grievances@bcbsma.com) — a DIFFERENT channel from general BCBS Member Services (800-257-8141). Reviews are conducted by professionals knowledgeable about the issues who were not involved in the prior decision and who do not work for anyone who was.
escalation_path.page: BD p.82 (unit, phone, e-mail); BD p.83 (reviewer independence)
escalation_path.audit_note: Gradeable: (1) rep should route to the Appeal & Grievance Program, not 'call this number back'; (2) reviewer independence is a stateable member protection. 'The same department reconsiders it' is 🟡 warning.

not_covered._rule: Facts searched for and NOT found in the plan documents — recorded honestly per the fail-loudly registry rule. Questions depending on these slots are EXCLUDED from call plans until sourced.
not_covered.member_services_hours: No hours of operation stated in Handbook or Benefit Description (Handbook contact page lists numbers only). Source from bcbsma.com before the call or drop the question — do not let the grader assume hours.
not_covered.language_access: No interpreter/TTY/translation provision surfaced from the Handbook text layer; the BD p.4-area nondiscrimination statement may carry language-assistance taglines the text layer missed — verify visually before grading any language-access question.
not_covered.claim_submission_deadline: How claims are filed is documented (provider files under payment agreements; member files with claim form in specific cases, BD p.79 area) but NO explicit member claim-filing deadline was found. Do not grade this question until located or dropped.

member_service_numbers._all_public: Public customer-service numbers from plan documents; no member PII.

BCBSMA 'Find a Doctor' support line
candidates.source: BD p.3 (8-1-2026 ed., Part 1 Member Services)

candidates.use: Campus clinical care under the Student Health Fee — not a benefits call center

dial_policy._rule: HARD campaign config, not guidance: the audit target for this plan is pinned; deny-listed numbers are blocked server-side at call initiation and cannot be substituted by any agent mid-run.
dial_policy.target_label: BCBS Member Services — verified against the Handbook IMPORTANT CONTACT NUMBERS page (HB PDF p.23)

deny_list.label: HUSHP Member Services (Harvard's own office)
deny_list.reason: THE CLIENT, not the audited party — dialing it would audit the wrong organization and constitute a serious incident. Likeliest mis-dial: it appears throughout the Handbook far more often than the BCBS line.

deny_list.label: Member Appeal and Grievance Program
deny_list.reason: Legitimate BCBSMA line but a specialist unit — a general benefits audit against it produces an unrepresentative sample. Only valid if a campaign explicitly targets appeals-unit handling.

critical_failures: Telling a member they have no appeal or that the process ends with BCBSMA's internal decision (external review exists: BD pp.84-86).

Telling a member the member alone can obtain a PA with no provider involvement, or conversely that the member has no role if the provider stalls (BD p.23 assigns both provider initiation and a member duty to request).

Quoting Medicare Part D clocks (72h/24h coverage determination) or ERISA clocks (15-day pre-service) for this plan's PA — wrong regulatory regime; plan standard is 2 working days from complete information (BD p.23).
Saying out-of-network pharmacy claims are covered (they are not — SoB p.6).
warning_failures: Quoting $3,000 in-network OOP max without explaining it is medical+Rx combined, or $1,700 without noting the separate $1,300 Rx maximum.
Saying a referral is required for specialists (none is — BD p.23).
Missing the ER copay waiver on admission/observation, the first-8-visits $0 mental-health benefit, or the HCCS higher-tier hospital copays.
Retail supply limit: answers should match the Schedule (30-day); the Summary's 60-day language is a known document conflict — a rep aware of the discrepancy scores a Pass with note.
